one_line: AI agents expand into shopping, code review and Linux security as U.S. export controls and state lawsuits tighten.

themes.title: Agents take on everyday and dev tasks
themes.text: Meta rolled out its Muse personal agent to UK adults for shopping and travel, Anthropic launched Claude Ship to review and approve GitHub pull requests, and OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source runtime that blocked a Java4Shell exploit in a controlled test without a restart.

stories.headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent in the UK for everyday tasks
Anthropic launches Claude Ship to auto‑review and approve GitHub pull requests
OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo for Linux security

themes.title: U.S. regulators and courts press AI firms
themes.text: Virginia and Oregon sued Musk companies over Grok's alleged lack of safety safeguards, the Commerce Department plans to add Megaspeed to the Entity List over alleged Nvidia chip export violations, and Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair after discussions with senior U.S. government officials.

stories.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue Musk companies over Grok sexualized images
U.S. Commerce Department to add Megaspeed to Entity List, restricting chip sales
Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and board chair

themes.title: Research on self-modifying and attackable agents
themes.text: Researchers introduced a 27B embodied agent that rewrites its own weights between tasks without training or gradients, presented FATCAT, a physical electromagnetic fault-injection attack that removes refusal in LLMs and vision-language models, and Google DeepMind detailed AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms.

stories.headline: Self-upgrading embodied agent rewrites its own weights from experience
FATCAT physical fault injection attacks eliminate LLM and vision-language model refusal
Google DeepMind details AlphaEvolve coding agent
